hints: A Type I error means rejecting $\text{H}_0$ when it is actually true. So start by stating $\text{H}_0$ (the population mean $\mu$ is still 35.2 minutes) and $\text{H}_1$ (the new route is quicker, so which way does $\mu$ move?).

Assume $\text{H}_0$ is true. Then the mean of 25 journeys has a normal distribution with mean 35.2 and standard deviation $\dfrac{5.6}{\sqrt{25}}$. Standardise the cut-off: $z = \dfrac{34.7 - 35.2}{5.6/\sqrt{25}}$.
Arvinder rejects $\text{H}_0$ when the sample mean is less than 34.7, so a Type I error has probability $\text{P}(Z < z)$ with your $z$. Your $z$ is negative, so use $\Phi(-a) = 1 - \Phi(a)$.
Find $\Phi$ of the positive value in a normal table or on your calculator, subtract it from 1, and round to 3 s.f.
walkthrough:
**What a Type I error is, and the hypotheses (earns the B1)**

A **Type I error** means rejecting $\text{H}_0$ when $\text{H}_0$ is actually true. Here, that means Arvinder decides the new route is quicker when really it is no quicker.

Let $\mu$ be the population mean journey time on the new route. If nothing has changed, $\mu$ is still the old mean. Arvinder hopes the time is **reduced**, so $\text{H}_1$ has a 'less than'.

$$\text{H}_0: \mu = 35.2 \text{ minutes}$$

$$\text{H}_1: \mu < 35.2 \text{ minutes}$$

**The distribution of the sample mean if $\text{H}_0$ is true**

We assume $\text{H}_0$ is true, because a Type I error is about what happens in that case. Single journey times are normal with standard deviation $5.6$. The question is about the **mean of 25 journeys**, $\bar{X}$ (the sample mean). A mean of 25 values varies less than a single value, so its standard deviation is divided by $\sqrt{25}$.

$$\bar{X} \sim \text{N}\left(35.2, \frac{5.6^2}{25}\right), \qquad \text{standard deviation} = \frac{5.6}{\sqrt{25}} = \frac{5.6}{5} = 1.12$$

**Standardise the cut-off value (first M1)**

Arvinder says the new route is quicker if $\bar{x} < 34.7$. To use the normal table we convert $34.7$ to a $z$-value, which says how many standard deviations it is from the mean.

$$z = \frac{34.7 - 35.2}{5.6/\sqrt{25}} = \frac{-0.5}{1.12} = -0.446$$

Common slip: forgetting the $\sqrt{25}$ and dividing by 5.6 instead. The $\sqrt{25}$ is needed for the method mark.

**Find the correct area (second M1)**

A Type I error happens when the sample mean is below $34.7$ even though $\text{H}_0$ is true, so we want the area to the left of $z = -0.446$.

$$\text{P}(Z < -0.446) = \Phi(-0.446)$$

Tables only list positive $z$, and the normal curve is symmetrical, so the area below $-0.446$ equals the area above $+0.446$:

$$\Phi(-0.446) = 1 - \Phi(0.446)$$

**Evaluate (A1)**

Table or calculator (normal cdf): $\Phi(0.446) = 0.6722$.

$$1 - 0.6722 = 0.3278$$

To 3 significant figures that is $0.328$. In words: if the new route made no difference, Arvinder would wrongly conclude it was quicker about 33% of the time.

hints: Compare the sample mean 34.5 with Arvinder's cut-off 34.7: does this result make him reject $\text{H}_0$ or not? Then recall which of the two decisions a Type II error needs.
walkthrough:
**Recall the two types of error**

- A **Type I** error is rejecting $\text{H}_0$ when it is true.

- A **Type II** error is **not rejecting** $\text{H}_0$ when it is false.

Notice that a Type II error can only happen when the decision was 'do not reject $\text{H}_0$'.

**Look at Arvinder's decision**

His rule is: if the sample mean is less than $34.7$, conclude the new route is quicker (reject $\text{H}_0$). His sample mean is $34.5$ and $34.5 < 34.7$, so he **rejects** $\text{H}_0$.

**Final answer**

His sample mean $34.5$ is below $34.7$, so $\text{H}_0$ is rejected. A Type II error can only be made when $\text{H}_0$ is **not** rejected, so it is impossible here.
